chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Harith ibn Muhammad from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had relations with his wife on a day he is making up from the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had relations with her before midday (al-zawal), there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day. And if he had relations with her on a day after midday, then he must give charity to ten poor people. If he is unable, he should fast one day in place of one day and fast three days as expiation for what he did.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast before or after midday?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *qada'* (making up the day) and *kaffarah* (expiation) based on the time of intercourse relative to *zawal* (midday). It establishes that pre-midday intercourse incurs only the missed day, while post-midday intercourse triggers a dual expiation: feeding ten poor people (or fasting three days if unable) plus an additional three days of fasting, reflecting the severity of breaking the fast's sanctity during daylight hours.
